subject.title: Feature: inbound 'reply in thread' / 'rit' user directive

question: Should OpenClaw add a built-in inbound natural-language reply-in-thread directive, and if so which trigger words and precedence rules are approved across supported channels?
rationale: The feature absence is clear, but automation should not choose global trigger vocabulary or cross-channel routing semantics because bad defaults can silently alter user text and message placement.

options.title: Approve a narrow built-in directive
options.body: Define the exact trigger set, likely excluding ambiguous bare `thread`, and specify precedence with `replyToMode`, explicit tags, existing threads, and top-level opt-outs before implementation.

options.title: Keep existing controls only
options.body: Treat `replyToMode`, channel-specific settings, message-tool targets, and explicit output tags as the supported threading controls and close or defer this feature.

options.title: Move to channel-specific design
options.body: Require channels or plugins to expose their own explicit reply-in-thread controls instead of adding one global natural-language parser.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow built-in directive
recommendation.body: Define the exact trigger set, likely excluding ambiguous bare `thread`, and specify precedence with `replyToMode`, explicit tags, existing threads, and top-level opt-outs before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is on the shared inbound/directive/reply-threading seams and repo product policy for channel behavior.
